sk.title: AI skills
src.allow_external: I agree that my queries (references, pseudonymised extracts) are sent to this service.
src.intro: Connectors to official databases of legislation and case law. Each source is checked (connection, search, reading a text) before it is enabled; nothing is sent without your consent to external data use.
src.no_key_needed: No key is needed for public access; an optional key raises the limits.
src.saved: Source saved. Run the check before enabling it.
src.title: Legal sources

step.agenda.explain: CalDAV is a way to connect to a calendar; its address is not necessarily that of your files. Authorised calendars are chosen one by one; none is selected automatically.
step.agenda.question: Which calendar do you use?
step.agenda.title: Calendar
step.agenda.todo: Set up the calendar in Settings › Connections: authorised calendars (CalDAV) or Google Calendar (OAuth).
step.agenda.unlocks: reading your events and, if you choose, adding deadlines.
step.agenda.where: Nextcloud Calendar: the calendar’s ⋯ menu › “Copy private link”. Google Calendar: a Google Cloud project with the Calendar API is required.
step.coordonnees.explain: The firm’s contact details can fill in the header and signature of your templates. You can check them before creating a document.
step.coordonnees.question: How can you be reached?
step.coordonnees.title: Your contact details
step.envoi.explain: The sending server (SMTP) is only used to send a message when you choose a send action. It is separate from receiving. Setting it up does not enable any automatic sending.
step.envoi.question: Do you want AxiorHub to be able to send a message when you decide?
step.envoi.title: Sending email (optional)
step.envoi.unlocks: sending a message after your confirmation.
step.envoi.where: Same section of your host’s help: SMTP server, port (587 with STARTTLS or 465 with direct TLS) and username.
step.facturation.explain: The connection checks access and the company in read mode. It creates no client or invoice and enables no sending.
step.facturation.question: Do you use Invoice Ninja?
step.facturation.title: Invoicing
step.facturation.todo: Invoice Ninja is set up in Settings › Connections, then “Tester Invoice Ninja”.
step.facturation.unlocks: linking clients, quotes, invoices, projects and tasks.
step.facturation.where: In Invoice Ninja: Settings › Account management › API tokens. Never share the internal APP_KEY.
step.fin.explain: Here are the available functions and the connections to complete. This summary contains no password, token, key or secret.
step.fin.question: Is everything ready?
step.fin.title: Summary
step.fin.where: You can return to each connection from Settings › Setup guide.
step.fonctions.explain: Only the steps for the chosen functions will be shown. The others remain available later in Settings.
step.fonctions.question: What would you like to use?
step.fonctions.title: Your functions
step.fonctions.unlocks: a path limited to what is useful to you.
step.fonctions.where: Nothing to look up: just tick what interests you.
step.ia.explain: Ollama runs AI models on a computer or server you control. Choose a fast model (sorting, extraction) and an analysis model (long texts, drafting); one model can fill both roles. External AIs (Claude, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Mistral) are set in “Providers and budgets”: they may receive the task data and charge for calls.
step.ia.question: Have you already installed Ollama?
step.ia.title: Artificial intelligence
step.ia.where: Official Ollama download and model list below; after installing, come back here and click “Check the connection” to refresh the list of models actually installed.
step.langues.explain: Interface language, drafting language and the law applicable to a case are separate: an English interface can prepare a French document for a case governed by French law.
step.langues.question: Which language do you want to work in?
step.langues.title: Language and time zone
step.langues.unlocks: correct dates and times, and suggested topics for the legal watch.
step.langues.where: The time zone is the firm’s (Europe/Paris for mainland France).
step.messagerie.explain: The receiving server (IMAP) lets AxiorHub read your messages and prepare drafts. Preferably use an app password separate from your main password.
step.messagerie.question: Which professional address do you use?
step.messagerie.title: Receiving email
step.messagerie.where: In your email host’s help, section “set up an email client”: IMAP server, port (993 = direct TLS, the most common; 143 = STARTTLS) and username.
step.modeles.explain: A tag is a marker telling the software where to place information: {{destinataire}} will be replaced by the chosen recipient. Your original template is never changed.
step.modeles.question: Do you want to produce letters in the firm’s layout?
step.modeles.title: Word templates
step.modeles.todo: Import your template in Firm documents: “Importer et prévisualiser” shows all pages.
step.modeles.unlocks: producing documents in the firm’s layout.
step.modeles.where: Your usual letter template, in DOCX format.
step.profil.explain: This information makes up your signature and the lawyer’s presentation given to the AI.
step.profil.question: Who are you?
step.profil.title: Your profile
step.profil.where: Your professional card and your bar directory.
step.sources.explain: An MCP connector gives AxiorHub organised access to a service’s search tools. Having a connector guarantees neither the completeness nor the applicability of a result.
step.sources.question: Do you have access to a legal sources service?
step.sources.title: Legal sources
step.sources.todo: Legal connectors are set up on the MCP connectors screen.
step.sources.where: Official sign-up pages below (GoodLegal, OpenLegi, LibreJustice, Legal Data Hunter).
step.stockage.explain: Your exhibits can be read and your drafts kept in the chosen space. A local folder belongs to the machine running AxiorHub: on a server, it is a folder on the server, not on your computer.
step.stockage.question: Where do you want to keep your documents?
step.stockage.title: Documents
step.stockage.where: Nextcloud: Personal settings › Security › “Create new app password” (required with two-factor authentication). The expected address is the base one (https://cloud.example.org), without /remote.php.
step.telephonie.explain: Twilio is a telephony service separate from Ollama. The HTTPS address that receives calls must be reachable by Twilio; a service limited to this computer (localhost) is not.
step.telephonie.question: Do you want administrative phone reception?
step.telephonie.title: Phone reception
step.telephonie.todo: Phone reception is set up on the Administrative reception screen.
step.telephonie.where: Twilio console: Auth Token (signature verification) and phone number.
step.veille.explain: The legal watch reads dated official feeds. A watch based on RSS feeds works without an Internet search key (Tavily).
step.veille.question: Which topics do you want to follow?
step.veille.title: Legal watch
step.veille.todo: Watch sources are set up on the Legal watch screen.
step.veille.unlocks: following legal news on your topics.
step.veille.where: Tavily: create an account, open your dashboard and copy an API key.
step.voix.explain: Installing Kokoro for your system, then choosing a voice for each language. Optional step.
step.voix.question: Would you like to listen to the briefing summary and the agent’s answers?
step.voix.title: Speech synthesis (Kokoro)
step.voix.todo: The voice is set in Settings › Voice.
step.voix.unlocks: reading aloud locally, without sending any text.
step.voix.where: Kokoro-FastAPI project (GitHub): Docker images and start scripts.
syn.queued: Exhibit summaries being prepared: the whole-case analysis will use them as soon as they are ready.
test.agenda.explain: The check lists the Nextcloud account’s calendars and checks that the ones you entered exist. No event is created.
test.envoi.explain: The check connects and logs in to the sending server, without sending any message.
test.facturation.explain: The check reads unpaid invoices read-only. No invoice, payment or reminder is created.
test.ia.explain: Three separate levels: service reachable, models installed, then, if you ask, a generation on a fictitious text.
test.messagerie.explain: The check logs in, opens the Drafts folder read-only and lists your folders. No message is read, marked as read or sent.
test.stockage.explain: The check reads the chosen root (without indexing your cases). “Also check writing” creates an announced technical file in the root, reads it back and deletes it.
test.telephonie.explain: The check verifies the callback address and computes a signature locally with your token, as each call will. No call is made.
vj.custom_feeds: Other RSS or Atom feeds (HTTPS addresses, one per line)
vj.empty_config: No watch topic. Enter your fields and keywords to receive sourced updates here.
vj.failed: The last collection failed: it will be retried.
vj.meta: Last successful check: {last} · last attempt: {attempt} · next: {next}
vj.not_run: First collection not yet carried out.
vj.nothing_new: Nothing new since the last check.
vj.refreshing: Collection started: new items will appear in a few minutes.
vj.settings_intro: Topics, sources and frequency of your watch. Each item is dated and linked to its source; an unavailable source is reported without blocking the others.
vj.tavily_intro: Tavily adds a sourced Internet search to the watch. Calls are capped and counted before each request.
vj.tavily_usage: Calls this month: {calls} ({uncertain} with an uncertain result).
vj.themes: Topics (one per line: name: keywords; sauf: exclusions)
vj.themes_hint: Commercial leases: commercial lease, rent, renewal; sauf: residential
vj.title: Legal watch
vj.use_connector: Also query the enabled legal source (recent decisions)
vj.use_tavily: Internet search with Tavily (key set by the administrator)
